claims.claim: Discovery here is something that happens to a person who is walking around Edinburgh in August
claims.reason: The source review never states when the festival takes place. 'in August' is an invented temporal detail imported from outside knowledge of the Edinburgh Art Festival's real-world calendar; nothing in the source text or the (empty) discovery packet establishes it.

claims.claim: And that second obligation is harder to discharge, because the subject is not in the room to say whether it has been met.
claims.reason: This is the article's own causal/comparative reasoning stated flatly as fact. The source says only that artists and institutions have a duty to viewers and subjects to tell hidden stories clearly; it says nothing about one obligation being harder than the other, nor does it generalise that subjects are absent or unable to assess the telling. True of the two dead artists named, but asserted universally. Resolving it would need the reviewer (or the packet) to actually make this claim rather than the article inferring it.
